Your impact begins here

Help build a stronger and more consistent approach to maintenance at Site Gentofte. As CMMS & Spare Parts Management Lead, you will help centralise and strengthen our computerised maintenance management system (CMMS) and spare parts management, supporting implementation of the Novo Nordisk Reliability and Maintenance blueprint. By connecting systems, master data, processes and people, you will help make maintenance activities more reliable and create practical improvements for daily production.

What you’ll bring

You bring hands-on expertise in SAP Plant Maintenance (PM) and Materials Management (MM), combined with an understanding of how maintenance systems and reliable master data support production. Just as importantly, you can turn complex requirements into clear ways of working and bring stakeholders with you.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• Proven experience in setting up, configuring and implementing SAP PM and SAP MM.

• In-depth knowledge of SAP PM and SAP MM and how they support maintenance and spare parts processes.

• At least two years of experience with reliability and maintenance of production equipment in a regulated environment.

• Experience with spare parts management, maintenance master data, task lists and related processes.

• Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to collaborate across different functions.

• The ability to structure your own work, drive several initiatives in parallel and communicate fluently in English.

You are motivated by creating structure, improving processes and helping colleagues use systems and data to support reliable production.

What you’ll do

Your focus will be on creating robust and consistent processes that work in practice. You will:

• Drive implementation and continuous improvement of CMMS and spare parts management processes in line with the Novo Nordisk Reliability and Maintenance blueprint.

• Support CMMS super users and colleagues responsible for spare parts management in establishing consistent ways of working.

• Act as a subject matter expert and facilitator for CMMS and spare parts management.

• Manage and improve master data for spare parts, maintenance schedules and equipment, working with stakeholders to maintain the required inputs.

• Work with production departments to support a seamless flow of maintenance activities and data and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Understand operational needs across production and translate them into improvements that create value in day-to-day work.

Who you’ll work with

You will join cGMP & Operations Support within Production Support at Site Gentofte. Production Support is a technical department of approximately 100 employees responsible for critical utilities and technical support for projects and operations.

Your immediate team has 15 colleagues with diverse educational backgrounds. One part of the team supports operations within CMMS and spare parts management across Site Gentofte, while another provides GMP support for utilities and quality processes across Production Support.

As CMMS and spare parts management are being centralised in the team, you will work closely with colleagues across production, maintenance execution and other support functions. You will join an environment with experienced colleagues where knowledge sharing and collaboration are part of everyday work.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to help shape a newly established function, including its structure, processes and ways of collaborating. The role combines development of maintenance capabilities with a close connection to daily production, giving you exposure to a broad stakeholder landscape across Site Gentofte.

You will work at the intersection of systems, maintenance and production, using your expertise to establish solutions that support reliable maintenance processes, high-quality master data and effective spare parts management.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200 to 838,100 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to use your SAP and maintenance expertise to strengthen CMMS and spare parts management at Site Gentofte, apply for the CMMS & Spare Parts Management Lead role by the 8th of November 2026.

For further information about the position, please contact Jonas Møllgaard Andersen at jyax@novonordisk.com

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

As Process Engineer in API Manufacturing in Kalundborg, you will help bring a new product into large-scale production. You will combine your chemistry or biochemistry knowledge with process data to understand the molecule, the reactions and the purification steps, and turn that insight into stable, compliant and efficient manufacturing. As the product moves from project into operations, you will take growing ownership and help more people living with diabetes and other serious chronic diseases get the treatment they need.

What you’ll bring

You understand manufacturing at a molecular, chemical and biochemical level, take ownership and stay constructive when priorities change. You will typically have:

• A Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in biochemistry, chemistry, biotechnology, biomedicine, chemical engineering or another relevant life-science discipline.

• Relevant experience from pharmaceutical manufacturing, API production, biotechnology or another chemistry-intensive production environment.

• Practical knowledge of one or more areas such as chemical modification, protein chemistry, organic chemistry, downstream processing, purification, filtration or HPLC.

• Working knowledge of cGMP in a regulated setting.

• Strong English communication skills and the ability to share knowledge, collaborate across functions and influence decisions.

• Curiosity, a proactive approach and enjoyment in solving complex challenges.

Useful, but not essential:

• Hands-on experience with deviations, investigations, change control, qualification or validation.

• Experience with data analysis to identify correlations and root causes in process data.

What you’ll do

You will strengthen product and process understanding in a state-of-the-art production environment and support the transfer of a new product from development into operations.

• Build a detailed understanding of how the molecule, chemical modification, protein chemistry and purification steps affect the final product.

• Analyse process data to find correlations and root causes, and turn the findings into practical improvements and monitoring.

• Support qualification and validation activities in line with cGMP requirements, and the implementation of new products and processes.

• Take ownership of product-related activities such as deviations, investigations, change requests, product transfers and continuous improvement.

• Share your specialist knowledge, contribute to technical decisions and help build capability in a growing team.

Priorities may shift as the organisation moves into operations. You will have the chance to help shape effective ways of working and how the team supports products and processes in the future.

Who you’ll work with

You will join a growing team in API Manufacturing at Novo Manufacturing Kalundborg, a leading production hub for insulins and GLP-1 analogues that support millions of people living with diabetes and other chronic diseases. Several colleagues are joining the area at the same time, so you can influence the team’s technical direction and its specialist culture from the start.

You will work with specialists in production, development, quality and engineering who continuously improve how we manufacture. Together you will connect scientific insight to practical decisions, with broad exposure to product changes, development activities and manufacturing challenges.

Please note: there will be manufacturing, storage or handling of semi-finished or finished GLP-1 products in the work location (building), regardless of whether you will directly handle the products.

What you can expect here

You will be supported to grow your skills while being trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard. Working across production, development, quality and engineering gives you broad experience of the value chain, and a growing team means room to build your expertise alongside colleagues who share it. Clear performance expectations help you deliver your best work and be recognised for it.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200 DK to 838,100 DKK corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Do you have experience with Reference Standards and are you passionate about creating a broad collaboration with Contract Manufacturing Organizations and internal stakeholders? Ready for your next career move? If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Reference Standard Specialist.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate Reference Standard Specialist to join our growing team. As a key member of the Reference Standard team, you will become point of contact in reference standard matters between Ascendis Pharma and Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) on specified projects. You will work to ensure continuous good relations and alignment with CMOs worldwide and stay updated with insights into their methods and processes together with our QC specialists. It is expected that in the collaboration you will contribute to areas such as analytical testing and test methods as well as regulatory guidelines and requirements on reference standards. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

Your typical workday will consist of discussions and support together with a small team of highly experienced colleagues. You will report directly to Therese Lindin, Associate Director for Reference Standards,who is based in Hellerup, and you will also be working at our headquarters in Hellerup.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Plan, coordinate and document activities regarding establishment, maintenance, re-supply, recalibration and distribution/shipping of reference standards and critical analytical substances

• Establish and maintain overview of reference standards for all purposes and product phases (development and commercial manufacturing) including storage location, stock, stability, expiry etc. for current standards as well as standards needed in the future to ensure availability of required standards

• Establish and maintain internal guidance (SOP or guides) for reference standards

• Make sure relevant updates of external legislation and guidelines for reference standards are implemented in the Ascendis Pharma QMS

• Contribute as an author on regulatory documents, such as IMPD's, IND's, NDA's and BLA's and provide answers to questions from authorities - in writing or face to face during inspections. Further, contribute to assessment of inspection readiness of CMO's

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a masters in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Engineering, or other relevant education - and a minimum of 5 years of experience from Biotech or Pharmaceutical industry working with reference standards.

Your knowledge and experience within the reference standard area will enable you to guide project teams at CMOs through conceptual as well as specific practical discussions. You have experience with coordination of reference standard activities, and experience with the commercial setup for resupply of reference standards. It will be an advantage if you have experience with analysis of large molecules, and preferably with polymers, proteins and/or peptides as well.

Furthermore, knowledge and practical experience in analytical sciences from the pharmaceutical industry within chromatographic analyses (HPLC) and bioassays, either from an analytical development laboratory or from a QC Laboratory will be an advantage.

Key competencies:

You have a structured and systematic approach to solving tasks and possess outstanding skills in collaboration and communication. As the job involves many stakeholders and coordination of activities both internally and externally, you thrive with being in contact with new people. You are a highly motivated individual who enjoys being challenged and working in collaborative environments. You possess a high energy level and focus on details.

To succeed in this role, we also expect you to have excellent abilities in terms of keeping an overview even with many active tasks at the same time. You are a strong team player, analytical, and have a can-do attitude. Criteria of success in the role will be to ensure efficient coordination of reference standard activities for development projects as well as post-approval resupply activities. Moreover, you are expected to actively contribute to the establishment of continuous improvements to our reference standard programs and establish close and high-standard collaborations with the CMOs and internally in Ascendis Pharma.

Travel: up to 10 days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time. To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Associate Director for Reference Standards, Therese Lindin, +45 40 40 32 65

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

FPRT is looking for a Senior Composite Process Technology Manager for our new composite production in Vojens, Denmark, and Moment Professionals manages the recruitment on our behalf. We are looking for a composite specialist with real depth in the technology who can convert transferred know-how into controlled, scalable and repeatable industrial processes. The role suits you if you want to build a production from the ground up and would rather build processes where little is written down yet than step into a production where everything is already in place.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the Chief Production Officer, Composite Manufacturing, and you build and lead the composite technology team of composite process engineers and materials and polymer engineers. You work closely with Production, Quality and NDT, HSE, Maintenance and Engineering, Planning and Supply Chain, and you support the competency and qualification standards for supervisors, technicians and operators together with Production and HR. You are the technical authority for composite manufacturing processes, with the mandate to define process parameters, technical standards and work instructions, and to require technical containment, a process review or a production stop when process integrity, product quality or safety is at risk.

Production starts from an existing process that is being transferred to Vojens, and experienced specialists from the group come to the site to hand it over. You lead the technical transfer and convert it into FPRT-controlled specifications, work instructions, training content and qualification requirements, and you define the technical requirements for equipment, tooling, fixtures, utilities and production conditions through trials, pilot builds and ramp-up. You make sure FPRT has clear local ownership of the critical processes and keeps the technical knowledge for the long term. From day one, you are expected to spot where a step can be done smarter and to have the composite understanding to back that view.

Your time is split between the desk and the floor. You own process flows, critical parameters, material requirements and process-control standards, and you define process qualification, inspection points, acceptance criteria and quality gates together with Quality and NDT. When a process starts to drift, you are the primary escalation point: you go to the floor, lead root-cause analysis, non-conformity investigations and corrective actions, and turn the lessons into updated standards and training. The weight of the role lies in the moulding stage and the material side of the process: resin systems, reinforcements such as carbon fibre, adhesives, curing and the conditions that decide whether porosity and voids are designed out or created. You need a sound grasp of finishing, but your depth is in why a part comes out of the mould as it does.

This is a greenfield site. New buildings are under construction on the site, systems are being selected, and support functions such as maintenance, IT and HR are being built in parallel. In the first period you will help shape how things are done well beyond your own field, and the composite team grows as production scales towards stable serial production.

The role is based in Vojens, and being on site is essential during the build-up. English is the working language in instructions and with colleagues across the group. Danish is a strong advantage in daily life on the floor, and if you are not fluent yet, your willingness to learn it counts.

And then there are the benefits:

Real authority over the processes you own, greenfield impact with no legacy to work around, a professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose, a modern office with gym, sauna and social spaces, and top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried a manager title or to come from defence. What matters is that you know composite technology in depth: why a resin system behaves as it does, what creates strength and what creates defects, and how the environment affects the part. You may come from composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence or another high-performance industry, and work today in process or manufacturing engineering, production, materials or as a technical composite specialist. You also take pride in:

• challenging an established method, including one handed over by experienced colleagues, and agreeing on a better answer together.

• taking ownership and making decisions where little is written down yet.

• going to the floor when a process drifts and staying until the root cause is found.

• turning know-how into standards, instructions and training that engineers and operators can work from.

• developing engineers through technical reviews, coaching and structured problem solving.

What you need to bring:

• Either a relevant technical degree or equivalent strong industrial experience, and at least five years in composite manufacturing, process engineering, manufacturing engineering or materials engineering.

• Practical experience with industrial manufacturing of fibre-reinforced composite components and thermoset resin systems such as epoxy, phenolic or other thermosets, and hands-on experience with one or more of resin infusion or transfer processes, filament winding, lay-up, moulding, curing, bonding or composite machining and finishing.

• A proven track record of developing, transferring, industrialising, qualifying or stabilising manufacturing processes into repeatable production, with a solid grip on process control, documentation, process risk assessment, root-cause analysis, non-conformity handling and technical change management.

• Experience leading, mentoring or coaching engineers and production specialists, or acting as their technical authority.

• Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is a strong advantage, or the willingness to learn it.

It is an advantage if you:

• come from advanced composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence, pressure vessels, automotive or another high-performance application.

• have worked with large or structurally critical components, such as aerospace and defence structures, casings, filament-wound products, UAV components or wind turbine blades.

• have taken part in a greenfield factory, a new production line, a technology transfer or a major ramp-up.

• live within commuting distance of 6500 Vojens, Denmark.

SORTH & CO is searching on behalf of Elopak Denmark A/S

PLANT DIRECTOR

Full responsibility for the performance of Elopak's production site in Lystrup, including safety, quality, delivery and cost. Succeeding a long-serving predecessor, you will have the mandate to shape culture, ways of working and leadership focus.

You will drive operational excellence based on TPM and serve as Managing Director of Elopak Denmark A/S, while leading major new projects launching in 2027.

Elopak is one of the world’s leading suppliers of carton packaging for liquid food products. Headquartered in Oslo and employing more than 2,850 people across 40 countries, Elopak is driven by a shared vision: creating sustainable packaging solutions that leave an undamaged world for future generations.

Elopak Denmark A/S is part of the global Elopak Group. It has a large production site in Lystrup near Aarhus with approximately 310 employees, and it works closely within a Nordic matrix structure across Technical Service, Aftermarket and Sales.

Read more about Elopak: https://www.elopak.com/

As Plant Director, you will lead the Danish production site with P&L responsibility. You will head a stable and well-functioning management team and focus on developing the culture, strengthening capabilities and shaping future leadership, while keeping operations stable and OEE high.

The Elopak Group has invested significantly in the Danish site, and new key projects will launch in Q1 2027. You will be responsible for ensuring smooth start-ups and efficient operations going forward. You will work closely with central functions as well as Sales and R&D in an international matrix organisation.

The Plant Director reports to the Global EVP Packaging and Procurement. The position is based full-time at the production site in Lystrup, Aarhus, Denmark.

Your responsibilities will include:

Site leadership

• Overall responsibility for site performance across safety, quality, delivery and cost

• Lead and develop the management team and serve as formal Managing Director of Elopak Denmark A/S

Strategic projects

• Oversee major projects and ensure smooth start-up and implementation

• Lead the introduction of new products and formats

Operational excellence

• Drive continuous improvement based on TPM, improving OEE and reducing downtime and waste

• Engage leaders at all levels as ambassadors for operational excellence

Safety and culture

• Lead the safety agenda and build a strong, proactive safety culture

• Act as a visible HSE role model on the shop floor

The suitable candidate

To succeed in this role, you know what it takes to run an efficient high-volume production on commercial terms, you lead in a way that engages an experienced team, and you excel across the full spectrum from strategy to daily operations.

We expect the successful candidate to bring:

• Several years of senior leadership experience in manufacturing, ideally as Plant Manager, Plant Director or Operations Director, from industries such as FMCG, food and beverage, packaging or paper – or from other comparable high-volume areas

• A proven track record of working with TPM standards and driving operational excellence, as well as leading new and complex projects

• Solid HSE experience, ideally from an organisation with a strong safety culture

• A visible, engaging leader who spends time on the shop floor, turns strategy into clear priorities and develops people and teams

• Combines high standards and accountability with a supportive, collaborative style, and works well across functions in an international matrix organisation

• Hands-on, solution-oriented and fact-based, with strong ownership and the ability to build trust at all levels

• Fluent in Danish and English, written and spoken

Elopak offers a central leadership position in an international organisation with strong values, high ambitions and a clear sustainability agenda. You will have significant influence on the future of the Danish site, and you will get the chance to shape both operational results and organisational capabilities.

The recruitment process is handled by SORTH & CO. If you have any questions, please contact Head of Search Sofie Kruse Møller, sofie@sorthco.dk or Partner Thomas Hansen, th@sorthco.dk.

Are you the kind of person who notices when something could be better, and has the drive to make it happen? At DISA, quality is not just a checkpoint at the end of the process. It is built into the way we design, source, produce and deliver world-class foundry machines. We are looking for a Quality Engineer who wants to be close to the product, close to production and close to the decisions that improve how we work.

This role is for someone who enjoys solving real quality challenges in a manufacturing environment. Someone who is structured, curious and persistent enough to follow an issue from first observation to sustainable improvement.

What You’ll Do

• Take ownership of quality improvements across supplier quality, production quality and internal quality processes.

• Handle non-conformities, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and ensure follow-up until issues are properly closed.

• Work closely with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers to identify risks, solve quality challenges and prevent repeat issues.

• Support and develop supplier quality performance through audits, structured follow-up, documentation and improvement plans.

• Use data, facts and structured problem-solving tools to analyze trends, set priorities and recommend practical quality improvements.

• Contribute to audits, customer requirements and management systems, with ISO 14001 as an area where you have basic knowledge or interest.

Why You’ll Love Working with Us

• A role where quality is at the center — not a side responsibility.

• The chance to work hands-on with complex, high-precision equipment and see the impact of your improvements in real production.

• A workplace where your structure, curiosity and follow-through help prevent issues before they reach the customer.

• Close collaboration with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers, so you can turn observations into practical improvements.

• The opportunity to help strengthen quality culture in a global industrial company with strong products, proud craftsmanship and long product lifetimes.

You will not be sitting far away from the product or the people making it. You will be part of the daily dialogue around quality, helping colleagues and suppliers understand what went wrong, why it happened and how we make sure it does not happen again.

Who You Are

• You have a background in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Production Technology or a similar field.

• You have experience with quality work in a manufacturing, production or industrial environment.

• You are motivated by root cause analysis, corrective actions and the satisfaction of closing issues properly.

• You understand supplier quality or are eager to work closely with suppliers on deviations, audits, documentation and improvement plans.

• You like being close to the shop floor and working with people across functions to solve practical quality challenges.

• You are analytical and structured, but also pragmatic enough to find solutions that work in real life.

• You follow through — because you know that quality improvements only matter when they are actually implemented and sustained.

• You have knowledge of ISO 14001 or an interest in building a basic understanding of environmental management systems.

If you are driven by quality, manufacturing and continuous improvement, and if you enjoy turning problems into clear actions and better ways of working, we would like to hear from you. You do not need to tick every box; what matters most is your quality mindset, your curiosity and your ability to follow through.

Want to know more? Ready to apply?

We will review candidates continuously, so please send your application as soon as possible. If you have any questions about the role, please contact Johnny Rasmussen at johnny.rasmussen@norican.com.

About the Role:

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

Architect, build, and scale AI systems that hold up in production

Take ownership of how AI is architected, built, and scaled across our products. You will design the agentic systems at the core of our pension and advisory platforms, with a focus on reliable and responsible AI.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to help lead our newly established AI team, working on our Life product for pension companies. The team is focused on the practical and responsible use of AI and is still in its early stages, so as a senior member you will play a defining role in setting the technical foundation, design patterns, and ways of working that the rest of the team builds on.

You will work closely with the AI Team Lead and Chief Architect, who own the overall architecture, helping shape the design within that direction. You will also be part of an agile team with a flat structure, where collaboration, curiosity, and continuous learning are central to the culture.

This role is primarily about designing and building agentic and LLM systems end to end, with a meaningful share of your time spent owning how we evaluate them and prove they hold up. It suits someone with 5+ years of relevant experience who wants to move beyond implementation into designing AI systems, and who enjoys raising the bar for the engineers around them.

Why this matters

This is core infrastructure, not edge tooling. Our Life product runs policy and capital administration for some of Europe’s largest pension providers, including PensionDanmark and APG, and is on track to support more than 8 million members and over €800bn in retirement assets.

The AI you design must meet that bar: fast and innovative, but also accurate, secure, and reliable enough for systems that people depend on for their financial security in retirement. Building it well and being able to prove it works, are two sides of the same job.

What you’ll do

As a senior member of the AI team, you will help shape how we build with Large Language Models and agentic systems across our products, contributing to high‑level design decisions, turning ambiguous business problems into robust system designs, and ensuring high‑quality coding standards and design. You will be hands‑on, with a real say in the architecture, standards, and technical judgement that guide the team.

In practice, you will:

Help shape the technical direction

• Contribute to the AI tech stack across our products: help define the high‑level system design, reference architectures, and design patterns the team builds on.

• Help shape AI strategy: identify where AI can create genuine value, frame the trade‑offs, and feed into a coherent, prioritised technical roadmap that fits our wider platform.

• Inform major architectural decisions: model and framework selection, build‑versus‑buy, and how AI components fit into our existing Java platform, integrate with surrounding systems, scale, and stay maintainable over time.

• Reason about trade‑offs in the open: weigh latency, cost, accuracy, security, and reliability, and explain and defend those choices to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Architect and build (hands‑on)

• Design LLM systems end to end: from retrieval, agent orchestration, and data pipelines through to deployment and monitoring.

• Design and build agentic systems: single‑ and multi‑agent, covering orchestration, tool use, action groups, knowledge‑base integrations, and patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation, and result aggregation for complex, reliable production workflows.

• Engineer RAG pipelines that connect agents to internal structured and unstructured data.

• Drive quality through design: prompt strategy, system prompts, and memory systems that produce hallucination‑resistant outputs with strong relevance and faithfulness.

• Make cost‑aware architectural choices: balancing latency, cost, and quality across model selection and orchestration patterns so what we ship is sustainable at scale.

• Set the standards for prompt strategy, RAG, orchestration, and cost management that the wider team adopts.

Evaluate and prove

• Build evaluation frameworks: eval sets, golden datasets, and LLM‑as‑judge pipelines, with offline regression suites wired into CI and online evaluation on production traces.

• Evaluate the whole agent, not just the answer: task success, trajectory and tool‑use correctness, and RAG faithfulness and grounding, so you know whether failures come from retrieval, reasoning, or generation.

• Measure what gates shipping: relevance, faithfulness, latency, cost, and reliability across repeated runs, turned into quality gates the team ships against.

Collaborate and grow the team

• Collaborate and mentor: work with the AI Team Lead, Chief Architect, senior developers, and product teams to translate business needs into working, well‑tested solutions, and support more junior engineers as the team grows.

What we’re looking for

You bring a strong technical foundation, hands‑on depth with modern AI tooling, and the judgement to design systems that hold up in the real world. You don’t need deep expertise in every area below, but we do expect real depth in agentic systems and AI architecture, backed by a solid grasp of how to evaluate what you build.

Required

• A master’s degree in computer science or a similar field, preferably with an AI focus.

• 5+ years building software, with significant hands‑on work applying Large Language Models.

• Strong proficiency in a statically typed, object‑oriented language, Java or C# (we build in Java). Python is welcome for demos, evaluation tooling, and experiments, but it is not our production language.

• Deep experience designing, building, and operating agent‑based systems, with hands‑on use of one or more orchestration frameworks (e.g. LangChain/LangGraph, Microsoft Agents, Claude Agent SDK, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel).

• A track record of designing and building AI systems, including how the components fit together, scale, and are maintained over time.

• Solid, practical experience with prompt strategy, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and the cost considerations of LLM usage and model selection.

• Working knowledge of LLM and agent evaluation: eval sets, LLM‑as‑judge, and the metrics that distinguish a good system from a confident‑but‑wrong one (faithfulness, relevance, task success, latency, and cost).

• Experience designing AI or backend systems that fit into a larger production platform, collaborating with senior engineers and architects to align on a shared technical direction.

• Strong communication skills to explain and defend architectural trade‑offs to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Nice to have

• Experience building automated evaluation pipelines or CI gates for AI systems.

• Familiarity with observability and tracing tooling for LLM applications (e.g. LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Braintrust).

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation, automation, and red teaming.

• Broader machine learning experience.

• Hands‑on experience building and integrating MCP servers.

• Experience working in regulated or high‑reliability domains such as finance, insurance, or healthcare.

Who you are

You are a confident, hands‑on engineer who takes ownership of complex and sometimes undefined problems, and who is just as comfortable designing a system as proving it holds up. You think in systems, balance pragmatism with quality, and care about building things that work in production rather than just in a demo. You lift the people around you, stay open to feedback, and bring strong technical judgement of your own. You are curious, persistent, and result‑oriented.
